ARTICLE 7 — CUSTOMER DATA, CARDHOLDER DATA, AND PCI-DSS

7.1 Ownership of Customer Data. As between the Parties, Customer shall retain all right, title, and interest in and to Customer Data. Provider acknowledges that Customer Data is the exclusive property of Customer.

7.2 Permitted Uses. Provider shall use and disclose Customer Data only as necessary to provide the Services to Customer in accordance with this Agreement and the applicable Order Form. Provider shall not use Customer Data for any other purpose, including without limitation product improvement, machine learning model training, marketing, or sale to third parties, except as expressly permitted by Customer in writing.

7.3 PCI-DSS Compliance. Provider shall maintain compliance with the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI-DSS) at the level required by the major card brands for the volume of card transactions processed through the Platform (which the Parties anticipate will be Level 1). Provider shall provide Customer with a current Attestation of Compliance from a Qualified Security Assessor on at least an annual basis and shall promptly notify Customer of any change in its PCI-DSS compliance status.

7.4 Cardholder Data Handling. Provider shall act as a "service provider" with respect to Cardholder Data within the meaning of PCI-DSS, and Provider's PCI-DSS compliance shall extend to all handling, storage, and transmission of Cardholder Data through the Platform and the Hardware Equipment. Provider shall not store any Cardholder Data outside of PCI-compliant scope. Cardholder Data shall be tokenized at the point of capture by the Hardware Equipment such that the Restaurant Location's network never transmits Primary Account Number information in the clear.

7.5 Brand Standards and Aggregate Reporting. The Parties acknowledge that the Brand Standards Module aggregates data across Customer's Restaurant Locations to compute brand-wide compliance metrics. Provider shall make this aggregated data available to Customer in the Brand Standards Module dashboard and reports, and shall not provide aggregated data identifiable to specific Restaurant Locations or Franchisees to any third party without Customer's prior written consent.

7.6 Security. Provider shall implement and maintain the safeguards required by PCI-DSS, including (a) encryption of Cardholder Data in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher; (b) encryption of Cardholder Data at rest using AES-256; (c) network segmentation isolating the cardholder data environment from other systems; (d) annual third-party penetration testing; (e) quarterly vulnerability scans by an Approved Scanning Vendor; (f) maintenance of SOC 2 Type II certification; and (g) a documented information security program reviewed at least annually.

7.7 Breach Notification. Provider shall notify Customer in writing of any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data without undue delay and in any event within seventy-two (72) hours of Provider's discovery. The notification shall include any information Provider reasonably has about the nature of the incident, the data involved, the affected Restaurant Locations and Franchisees, and the actions Provider is taking. Provider shall also notify the relevant card brands and acquiring banks as required by PCI-DSS.

7.8 Subprocessors. Provider shall maintain a list of subprocessors that have access to Customer Data on Provider's Customer Trust Portal. Provider shall provide Customer with at least thirty (30) days prior written notice of any addition or change to a subprocessor that has access to Cardholder Data. Customer may object to any new or changed subprocessor on reasonable security grounds.

7.9 Data Residency. Provider shall store and process Customer Data within data centers physically located in the contiguous United States.

7.10 Data Return and Deletion. Upon expiration or termination of an Order Form, Provider shall, at Customer's election, make Customer Data attributable to such Order Form available for export by Customer in a commercially reasonable, machine-readable format for a period of sixty (60) days, or permanently delete such Customer Data from production systems within thirty (30) days. Cardholder Data shall be deleted in accordance with PCI-DSS retention requirements.

ARTICLE 7 — STUDENT DATA AND PRIVACY

This is the most important article in this Agreement, so we kept the language plain. If anything in this Article 7 conflicts with anything elsewhere in the Agreement, this Article 7 wins.

7.1 You own Student Data. The District owns all Student Data. We do not own it, we do not have any rights to it beyond the limited permission you give us in Section 7.2, and we will not claim a right to it later.

7.2 Why we touch Student Data. You give us permission to host, store, process, and display Student Data only to provide the BrightStep Platform to you. Specifically, we will not (a) use Student Data to advertise or market to students or parents, (b) sell Student Data, (c) use Student Data to build user profiles for non-educational purposes, or (d) use Student Data to train any artificial intelligence model unless you give us specific written permission for a specific project.

7.3 FERPA. We are acting as a "school official" with "legitimate educational interests" under FERPA, 34 C.F.R. § 99.31(a)(1)(i)(B). That means we are subject to all the same restrictions on use and re-disclosure of education records that apply to your own employees. We will not re-disclose Student Data to anyone except the limited subprocessors we list at brightstep.com/subprocessors, and even then only as needed to run the BrightStep Platform.

7.4 COPPA. Many of your students are under 13. We rely on you to provide the parental consent that COPPA requires for school use, and we limit our collection and use of personal information from students under 13 to what is reasonably necessary for the educational service. We do not require students to disclose more personal information than is reasonably necessary to participate in an activity.

7.5 Ohio Student Data Laws. We comply with SOPIPA and AB 1584. We do not engage in targeted advertising, do not use covered information to amass a profile, and do not sell covered information. We will delete your students' covered information within forty-five (45) days of your written request.

7.6 Security. We protect Student Data with what we believe are reasonable security measures, including:

(b) encryption of Student Data at rest using AES-256;
(c) role-based access controls so only employees who need to see Student Data can see it;
(d) annual third-party penetration tests; and

7.7 Breach. If we discover a security incident that compromises Student Data, we will tell you in writing within seventy-two (72) hours, even if we are still investigating. The notice will tell you what happened, who we think was affected, what data was involved, and what we are doing about it. We will pay the reasonable costs of any breach notifications you have to send out under Ohio law if the incident was caused by something we did wrong. We will help your team investigate.

7.8 Where Student Data lives. We store Student Data in data centers inside the contiguous United States. We do not move it outside the United States. If we ever need to change that, we will get your written approval first.

7.9 Subprocessors. We use a small list of service providers (like our cloud hosting provider and our error tracking provider) that touch Student Data. The current list is at brightstep.com/subprocessors. We give you thirty (30) days notice before we add or change a subprocessor that handles Student Data, and you can object on reasonable security grounds. If we cannot resolve your objection, you can terminate this Agreement and get a prorated refund.

7.10 Audit. Once per year, with at least thirty (30) days notice, you (or a third party you choose, under NDA) can review our security practices. We will respond to a reasonable security questionnaire. For a deeper audit (like an on-site visit), we will charge you our reasonable costs and you will follow our protocols.

7.11 Data return and deletion. When this Agreement ends, you have ninety (90) days to export Student Data using our self-service export tool at no charge. ARTICLE 7 — CUSTOMER DATA, PRIVACY, AND HIPAA

7.1 Ownership of Customer Data. As between the Parties, Customer shall retain all right, title, and interest in and to Customer Data, including all PHI. Provider acknowledges that Customer Data is the exclusive property of Customer.

7.2 Business Associate Status. The Parties acknowledge that, in providing the Services, Provider shall be acting as a "business associate" of Customer, as that term is defined under HIPAA. The BAA attached hereto as Exhibit A is incorporated by reference and constitutes the binding Business Associate Agreement between the Parties. In the event of a conflict between this Article 7 and the BAA with respect to PHI, the BAA shall control.

7.3 Permitted Uses. Provider shall use and disclose Customer Data, including PHI, only as permitted by HIPAA, the BAA, this Agreement, and the applicable Order Form. Provider shall not use Customer Data for any other purpose, including without limitation product improvement, machine learning model training, marketing, or sale to third parties, except as expressly permitted by Customer in writing.

7.4 Security. Provider shall implement and maintain administrative, physical, and technical safeguards designed to comply with the HIPAA Security Rule (45 C.F.R. Part 164, Subpart C), including without limitation (a) encryption of PHI in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher; (b) encryption of PHI at rest using AES-256; (c) role-based access controls aligned with the Authorized Site and Authorized User structure on each Order Form; (d) annual third-party penetration testing; (e) maintenance of HITRUST CSF certification or equivalent; and (f) a documented information security program reviewed and updated at least annually.

7.5 Breach Notification. Provider shall notify Customer in writing of any "Breach" of "Unsecured Protected Health Information" (as both terms are defined under 45 C.F.R. § 164.402) without unreasonable delay and in any event within the timeframe set forth in the BAA, which shall not exceed seventy-two (72) hours of Provider's discovery of such Breach.

7.6 Right to Audit. Once per calendar year, upon at least sixty (60) days prior written notice, Customer (or a third-party assessor engaged by Customer and bound by reasonable confidentiality obligations) shall have the right to audit Provider's compliance with this Article 7 and the BAA, at Customer's expense. Customer shall conduct any audit during normal business hours, in a manner that does not unreasonably interfere with Provider's operations, and in compliance with Provider's reasonable security protocols. The frequency of audits may be increased without limitation following a Security Incident or upon the request of any regulator with jurisdiction over Customer.

7.7 Subprocessors. Provider shall maintain a list of subprocessors that have access to PHI on Provider's Customer Trust Portal, which list is incorporated by reference into the BAA. Provider shall provide Customer with at least thirty (30) days prior written notice of any addition or change to a subprocessor that has access to PHI. Customer may object to any new or changed subprocessor on reasonable security or compliance grounds. If the Parties cannot resolve Customer's objection in good faith, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form for cause and receive a prorated refund of any prepaid Subscription Fees.

7.8 Regulator Cooperation. Provider shall cooperate with any audit, inquiry, or investigation by the Department of Health and Human Services Office for Civil Rights, any state attorney general, or any other regulator with jurisdiction over Customer's handling of PHI. Provider shall make available to Customer such information as Customer may reasonably require to respond to any such regulatory inquiry.

7.9 Data Residency. Provider shall store and process Customer Data within data centers physically located in the contiguous United States. Provider shall not transfer Customer Data outside of the United States without Customer's prior written consent.

7.10 Data Return and Deletion. Upon expiration or termination of an Order Form for any reason, Provider shall, at Customer's election: (a) make Customer Data attributable to such Order Form available for export by Customer in a commercially reasonable, machine-readable format for a period of ninety (90) days following expiration or termination; or (b) permanently delete such Customer Data from Provider's production systems within thirty (30) days of expiration or termination, with backup deletion to follow in accordance with Provider's standard backup retention schedule.

ARTICLE 6 — SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT AND SUPPORT

6.1 Uptime Commitment. Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to make the Platform available with a Monthly Uptime Percentage of at least 99.5%, calculated as: (Total Minutes in Month - Excluded Minutes - Downtime Minutes) / (Total Minutes in Month - Excluded Minutes), expressed as a percentage. The Parties acknowledge that the Platform is designed to operate in offline mode at the terminal level for short periods of time, and that brief cloud connectivity interruptions affecting reporting and synchronization shall not generally affect order entry and payment processing functionality at the Authorized Locations.

6.2 Excluded Downtime. The following shall not be counted as Downtime: (a) scheduled maintenance windows, which shall be conducted between 3:00 a.m. and 5:00 a.m. Eastern Time and shall not exceed four (4) hours per calendar month; (b) emergency maintenance with as much advance notice as is reasonably practicable; (c) downtime caused by Customer's acts or omissions, including loss of internet connectivity at any Authorized Location; (d) downtime caused by Force Majeure Events; (e) downtime caused by failures of third-party services, including without limitation Payment Processors; and (f) downtime caused by Customer's use of third-party hardware that does not meet Provider's specifications.

6.3 Service Credits. If the Monthly Uptime Percentage falls below 99.5%, Customer shall be entitled to receive service credits as follows: (a) below 99.5% but at or above 99.0%: a service credit equal to five percent (5%) of one-twelfth (1/12) of the annual Subscription Fee; (b) below 99.0% but at or above 98.0%: ten percent (10%); (c) below 98.0%: twenty-five percent (25%). Service credits shall not be paid in cash and shall not exceed in the aggregate twenty-five percent (25%) of the annual Subscription Fee in any Subscription Year.

6.5 Severity Levels. Provider shall categorize support issues using the following severity levels: Severity 1 (any condition preventing order entry or payment processing at any Authorized Location during business hours), Severity 2 (significant degradation affecting reporting, inventory, or other non-critical functions), Severity 3 (limited functionality issue with workaround), and Severity 4 (general inquiry or feature request).
